result.title: Can an LVLM Perceive Event Boundaries Like a Human?
result.summary: Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) reason effectively about video content, but whether they perceive its event boundaries in a manner consistent with humans remains unclear. We first investigate this through Generic Event Boundary Detection (GEBD), which identifies event boundaries naturally perceived by humans in continuous video, without relying on predefined event categories. On Kinetics-GEBD dataset, LVLMs miss many boundaries when predicting directly from frames, but effectively refine candidates proposed by an unsupervised discovery method, achieving state-of-the-art unsupervised GEBD performance. We extend this discovery-refinement approach to hour-long egocentric video, where boundary discovery requires a broader semantic scale and whole-video LVLM refinement becomes impractical. We address these challenges through coarse-to-fine temporal discovery and localized LVLM accept/reject judgments. Human evaluation shows that the LVLM's agreement with group consensus falls within the range observed among human annotators, with disagreements concentrated on low-consensus cases. Using this pipeline, we construct EgoBoundary, a benchmark for event boundary detection in hour-scale egocentric video. Representative supervised and unsupervised methods degrade substantially on EgoBoundary, highlighting the challenge of long-horizon event boundary detection.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文考察 LVLM 是否像人一样感知视频事件边界：在 Kinetics-GEBD 上先用无监督方法提出候选、再由 LVLM 精化，取得无监督 GEBD 的 SOTA，并将该「发现—精化」流程扩展到小时级第一人称视频（粗到细时间发现＋局部接受/拒绝判断），最后构建 EgoBoundary 基准并显示现有方法显著退化。
AI.relevance_reason: 与主线不直接重合，但其「无监督候选生成＋LVLM 局部接受/拒绝」式精化和粗到细时间定位，可供核查 LVR 中视觉证据筛选与候选验证、以及何时停止/切分推理状态的设计线索。
